Laura/Vivek — attaching my initial technical notes below. High level: Redwood processes tokenized user inputs for inference; customer-configured retention is configurable per-DPA; default telemetry is aggregated and pseudonymized. We do have a small set of US-based support subprocessors for hardware maintenance and observability ingestion; these are covered by SCCs and our DPA plus contractual PII access restrictions.

Highlights (summary):
- Data flows: EU region requests are served from eu-west region by default. Where customers enable cross-region fallback or Dedicated in another region, we document that explicitly in the DPA.
- Subprocessors: list in Annex A of our DPA; we will provide per-request exportable list.
- Encryption: TLS1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest; customer KMS support (bring-your-own-key) for Private deployments.
- Logging: access logs retained 90 days by default; audit logs retained 1 year for enterprise customers on agreement.

I attached a CSV-matrix (redwood_security_controls_matrix.csv) and a draft PDF with narrative answers (redwood_tia_response_draft.pdf).

Sven — quick answers below and happy to expand in the walkthrough on Oct 19 at 10:00 CEST (invite sent separately).

1) US subprocessors and cleartext access: Any US-based maintenance or observability subprocessors have no routine access to cleartext customer inference inputs. In standard hosted flows we tokenize and limit payloads before sending telemetry; access is restricted by role-based controls and requires explicit escalation. For customers that require absolute limits on transfer scope we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments and/or customer-managed keys.

2) Audit log retention: Yes — retention windows are configurable via contract. Default is 90 days, but we can contractually extend to 2 years for specified log classes for enterprise agreements. Note that extended retention may have cost implications; we'll include pricing in the contract addendum.
